issue_context.title: AddUserSecrets optional parameter not working as expected
issue_context.body:
### Description

When using the AddUserSecrets method as follows, I would expect an exception to be thrown if the correlated secrets.json file is missing.  However, the internal secrets provider continues to indicate that it is optional, and no exception is thrown.

`config.AddUserSecrets<Startup>(optional: false);`

### Configuration

.NET Core 3.1.9
Windows 10
x64

### Other information

I posted [this issue on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64647810/can-the-user-secrets-file-be-declare-as-required-for-an-asp-net-core-applicati) and received confirmation from other users that they are seeing similar behavior.  One user pointed out that [the source itself](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1ade5327c94d1b67622705b9f9b76fac4b49e677/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.UserSecrets/src/UserSecretsConfigurationExtensions.cs#L192) uses the parameter only for checking the project setting, but not for the existence of an actual secrets file, which contradicts the behavior of the underlying JsonConfigurationProvider.
